title: DNA Methylation from Long Reads
eyebrow: Lesson 5 · marks on the DNA that the letters do not show
intro: Many cytosines in an animal's genome carry a small methyl group. It does not change the sequence, but it helps keep transposons silent, marks which parent a gene copy came from, changes with tissue and age, and over evolutionary time wears CpG sites away. Long-read machines can see the mark directly on each native DNA molecule. This lesson starts with the biology and how it differs between animal groups, then shows how nanopore and PacBio reads detect methylation and how the calls are stored, how to turn reads into one methylation level per CpG, how to get methylation for each parental copy, how to read it against genes, transposons and satellites, how to compare samples and what epigenetic age clocks need, and how to check and view the results.

Our own long reads of one rodent species (species A) arrived as plain FASTQ without raw signal or modification tags, so no methylation can be called from them; the lesson uses that as its cautionary example of what to ask a sequencing provider to keep, and works with toy data and public human data instead. The footprint of past methylation is still visible in our data: CpG sites in young bat SINEs change about six times faster than other sites. Bisulfite and array methods are only outlined here, and SINEs and satellites themselves are treated in depth in a later lesson. Hover over a dotted term to see what it means.

steps.title: What methylation is and why zoologists care
steps.what: 5mC at CpG, the enzymes, methylation level, 5hmC and 6mA; how lineages differ; CpG depletion and islands; imprinting, X inactivation, clocks and inheritance.

steps.title: How long reads see methylation
steps.what: Current and polymerase timing, calling modified bases, the MM/ML tags, why FASTQ loses everything, and what to ask the provider to keep.

steps.title: From reads to per-site methylation
steps.what: Aligning without losing the tags, counting reads per CpG, pass thresholds, the bedMethyl columns, and how many reads a level needs.

steps.title: Methylation on each parental copy
steps.what: Phasing and haplotagging reads, per-copy pileups, imprinting and X inactivation, and why HP1 is not the mother.

steps.title: Repeats, genes and the genome
steps.what: The bimodal mammalian pattern, promoters and gene bodies, methylation by transposon age, satellites, and mappability.

steps.title: Comparing samples
steps.what: Differentially methylated regions, replicates versus reads, effect size versus significance, confounders, and epigenetic clocks.
steps.tools: modkit dmr · DSS · dmrseq · methylKit · metilene

steps.title: Quality checks and viewing
steps.what: Checking tags and models, call probabilities, coverage and strands, controls, IGV colouring, plots, and what to keep from every run.
